info.name: User
info.description:
Sign-up, email verification, and user records.

## Sign-up flow
```
POST /users/register          -> { token }      (purpose token, 10 min)
         |
         v
POST /users/verify-email-otp  (Bearer: that token, body { otp })
         |
         v
   account verified -> POST /auth/login
```
A user who has not verified cannot log in: login answers 403 `Please verify your email before logging in.`

## Already-registered emails
If the email exists but was never verified, register does **not** fail. It updates the record, sends a fresh OTP and returns a new token, so an abandoned sign-up can simply be restarted. It only returns 409 when the email belongs to a verified account.

request.description:
Creates the account and emails a 6-digit OTP.

**Body**
| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| name | string | yes | the Discord username from the sign-up form |
| email | string | yes | must be a valid address |
| password | string | yes | at least 6 characters |
| phone | string | no | not collected by the Avora sign-up form |

**Returns** — only the token, nothing else:
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "statusCode": 201,
  "message": "An OTP has been sent to your email. Please verify it to complete registration.",
  "data": { "token": "eyJhbGci..." }
}
```
Hold this token (sessionStorage is a good place) — the next call needs it as a bearer token. It expires in 10 minutes.

**Errors**
| Status | message |
|---|---|
| 409 | User with this email already exists |
| 400 | validation errors from class-validator |

**Note:** the email is sent *after* the response returns, so this call is fast and never blocks on SMTP. In development the OTP is also printed to the server terminal:
```
[OtpService] OTP for newuser@example.com: 123456
```

The test script saves the token as `verifyEmailToken`.

Confirms the email address and activates the account.

**Auth:** the token from Register — **not** a session token.

**Body:** `{ "otp": "123456" }` — the OTP is **6 digits**.

**Returns** the created user:
```json
{
  "data": {
    "id": 21,
    "email": "newuser@example.com",
    "name": "robin.keyz",
    "phone": "",
    "role": "user",
    "isDeleted": false,
    "isEmailVerified": true,
    "createdAt": "2026-10-19T10:12:00.000Z",
    "updatedAt": "2026-10-19T10:14:30.000Z"
  }
}
```

**Errors**
| Status | message |
|---|---|
| 404 | OTP not found! |
| 400 | OTP has expired |
| 400 | Wrong OTP |
| 400 | Email is already verified. |
| 401 | Invalid or expired token |

This does **not** log the user in. Send them to the login screen afterwards.

Sends a fresh registration OTP. No body.

**Auth:** the token from Register — it stays valid, so reuse the same one.

For the "Didn't receive code? Resend" link.

If the 10-minute token has expired, call Register again with the same details — the account is unverified, so it is allowed and you get a new token.

The signed-in user's full record.

**Auth:** session token.

Same data as `GET /auth/me`, plus `isDeleted`, `createdAt` and `updatedAt`. Use whichever reads better in your code.

query.description: Partial match across name, email and phone.
Field name. Prefix with - for descending.
Exact-match filter on any column. Remove if not needed.

request.description:
Paged, searchable user list. **Super Admin only.**

**Auth:** session token of a `superAdmin`. Anyone else gets 403 `You are not authorized.`

**Query parameters**
| Param | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| page | 1 | |
| limit | 10 | |
| searchTerm | — | matches name, email or phone; multiple words all have to match |
| sort | — | `name` ascending, `-name` descending |
| fields | — | comma separated column list |
| *anything else* | — | treated as an exact-match filter, e.g. `role=user` |

**Returns** — note `pagination` sits beside `data`, not inside it:
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "statusCode": 200,
  "message": "User list retrieved successfully",
  "pagination": {
    "page": 1,
    "limit": 10,
    "totalItem": 42,
    "totalPage": 5
  },
  "data": [ { "id": 13, "name": "Admin", "...": "..." } ]
}
```

One user by id.

**Auth:** any signed-in user.

The id must be a whole number — `/users/abc` returns 400 `Validation failed (numeric string is expected)`.

**Errors**
| Status | message |
|---|---|
| 404 | User not found. |

Soft delete — sets `isDeleted = true`. The row stays in the database and the user can no longer sign in.

**Auth:** session token of a `superAdmin`.

**Errors**
| Status | message |
|---|---|
| 404 | User not found. |
| 400 | User is already deleted. |
| 403 | Cannot delete a superAdmin account. |

Only ordinary `user` accounts can be deleted; a Super Admin cannot be removed this way.
